# Harmonize architecture rules

<!-- Generated by harmonize-skills from the Harmonize rule sources. Do not edit; regenerate with `swift package --package-path SwiftPackages/HarmonizeRules harmonize-skills`. -->

This project enforces its architecture with [Harmonize](https://github.com/perrystreetsoftware/Harmonize) lint rules. The rules run as unit tests. CI fails on any violation. Run the rules after you implement a task.

## Rules by layer

Before you write code in a layer, read its file. Each file lists the rules of that layer. Each rule file gives the rationale, the fix, and examples.

- [datasource](references/datasource.md) (1 rule): Rules for data sources and their interfaces. Read before you create or change a data source.
- [designsystem](references/designsystem.md) (17 rules): Rules for the design system: atoms, molecules, organisms, templates, roles, and tokens. Read before you create or change a UI component.
- [di](references/di.md) (2 rules): Rules for dependency injection: module registration and injected types. Read before you register or inject a dependency.
- [mappers](references/mappers.md) (2 rules): Rules for mappers between DTOs, domain models, and UI models. Read before you create or change a mapper.
- [meta](references/meta.md) (1 rule): Rules about the lint rules themselves. Read before you write a lint rule.
- [models](references/models.md) (3 rules): Rules for DTOs, domain models, and state types. Read before you create or change a model.
- [repositories](references/repositories.md) (3 rules): Rules for repositories. Read before you create or change a repository.
- [tests](references/tests.md) (3 rules): Rules for unit tests. Read before you write a test.
- [ui](references/ui.md) (8 rules): Rules for screens, adapters, and view modifiers. Read before you create or change a view.
- [usecase](references/usecase.md) (4 rules): Rules for use cases. Read before you create or change a use case.
- [viewmodel](references/viewmodel.md) (9 rules): Rules for ViewModels and their state. Read before you create or change a ViewModel.

Harmonize also enforces the rules that are not listed here. Their test failures explain the fix.
